thought_vector_text: For dense React Three Fiber InstancedMesh scenes on mobile, decouple visual geometry from touch geometry: synchronize an invisible hit layer, preserve instanceId, rank hits by screen-space touch intent, and prove selection with real Android taps.
context_environment: seed-skill:r3f-dense-instanced-node-ui. Noosphere's Android WebView rendered glowing nodes whose perceived Bloom footprint was larger than the raycast mesh; overlapping particle layers and transparent display overlays also made taps select the wrong node.

evidence.symptom: Visible glowing nodes on Android could be tapped without opening details, or the tap selected a different node than the one nearest the user's finger.
evidence.root_cause: Bloom enlarged the perceived footprint beyond the compact InstancedMesh raycast geometry; transparent transition layers could still intercept input; competing particle layers were ordered by world depth instead of touch-center precision.
evidence.fix: Keep compact visual instances, add a synchronized invisible low-poly hit layer, preserve event.instanceId, stop propagation, use a screen-space perceptual score across layers, and make decorative DOM transition layers non-interactive.
evidence.verification: A Pixel 5 regression and a real Android WebView ADB test tapped projected dynamic node coordinates, confirmed the pointer target was CANVAS, matched the selected instanceId to the intended node, opened the detail panel, and found no fatal logcat entry.
evidence.applies_when: Use when a mobile R3F or Three.js dense node cloud displays a target that is difficult to select precisely, especially with InstancedMesh and postprocessing glow.
evidence.avoid_when: Do not apply to ordinary DOM hit testing or to sparse individual meshes until event propagation and overlay interception have been measured.
